subject: Renewal negotiation: pricing reconciliation + credit bundling
messages:
From: Maya Torres <maya@cloudvest.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal planning — pricing flexibility and credits

Hi Rishi,

Hope you’re well. Our renewal for CloudVest is coming up in mid-November and I wanted to kick off pricing discussions so we can align procurement and legal early. High-level asks from our side: 

- We’re evaluating a 12 vs 24 month renewal window and need clarity on how discounts and credits map to term length.
- We’d like a temporary price-hold for q1 if we commit to a minimum baseline.
- Can you outline an option that includes an upfront credit bucket to cover burst months?

I’ve attached the Q3 usage export for context (CSV) — it shows two clear surge months where burst credit would help.

Can you share 2–3 concrete options (pricing + credits + billing terms) by EOD Thursday so procurement can review?

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Torres
Head of Cloud Procurement, CloudVest
maya@cloudvest.com

Attachment: cloudvest_usage_Q3.csv (stub)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Torres <maya@cloudvest.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T11:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — pricing flexibility and credits

Thanks Maya — appreciate the usage file. Looping in Monica and Laura; they’ll help with capacity and approval flow.

Quick read and two preliminary options below; I’ll send a short term sheet (v3) after you confirm which path you want us to price in detail.

Option 1 — 12 month (conservative, fastest turnaround)
- 10% list discount on current committed unit price
- $75k upfront credit bucket to cover burst months (applies to token overages, expires month 12)
- Price-hold for Q1 on current per-token price (conditional on baseline commit)
- Net-45 invoicing

Option 2 — 24 month (better unit economics)
- 16% list discount
- $150k credit bucket, phased (50% immediate, 50% at month 12)
- Firm 12-month price-hold, then annual CPI-based adjustments capped at 3%
- Dedicated burst pool with negotiated latency SLOs (monica, see technical note below)

Asks from our side to firm up numbers:
- Confirm preferred term (12 vs 24)
- Target annual baseline (tokens/month) to set the commit band
- Any required billing/legal constraints (e.g., PO cadence, invoice contacts)

I’ve attached a draft term sheet (redwood_term_sheet_v3.pdf) with placeholders for baseline and credit allocation. If you want, we can map Option 2 to a phased onboarding plan and slip in a canary capacity window for Q4.

I’ll sit on the procurement timeline — planning a 48-hour review from legal once you tell us which option to finalize.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: redwood_term_sheet_v3.pdf (stub)

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>, Maya Torres <maya@cloudvest.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T08:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — pricing flexibility and credits

Adding a technical lens here so procurement knows the operational tradeoffs.

- Burst credits: we apply credits to on-demand token usage automatically; credits do not reduce committed capacity billing, only overage.
- Dedicated burst pool (Option 2): requires a short provisioning window (2–3 weeks) and a small on‑demand ingress buffer. We can guarantee a 95th percentile latency target for the burst pool with an SLA addendum.
- If you want a price-hold for Q1, we recommend a minimal commit floor (e.g., 70% of your current average) so that we can guarantee capacity and avoid excessive autoscale churn.

If it helps, I can run a capacity forecast matching your Q3 spikes to the two options and return a recommended baseline.

— Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
monica@redwoodinference.com

From: ProcureOps <procureops@cloudvest.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Torres <maya@cloudvest.com>, Legal <legal@cloudvest.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — pricing flexibility and credits

Rishi / team — procurement here. A few constraints from our side before we can sign off on any pricing: 

1) Invoicing: CloudVest needs Net-45 terms and a single invoice per quarter covering committed + overage.
2) Security: we have a short vendor addendum (data residency clause) that must be attached to the final agreement.
3) Contract: prefer a 60-day signature window; any pricing that requires early payment must be explicit.

Also, we ran the Q3 usage you sent and would prefer Option 2 (24m) if you can: 
- Provide the $150k credit bucket structure in the term sheet, and
- Confirm that phase 1 (50% of credits) is available at signature.

Please send the updated term sheet with the procurement redlines and we’ll circulate to legal.

ProcureOps (on behalf of CloudVest)
procureops@cloudvest.com

On Thu, Oct 20, 2026 at 11:37 AM Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Thanks Maya — appreciate the usage file. Looping in Monica and Laura; they’ll help with capacity and approval flow.
> 
> Quick read and two preliminary options below; I’ll send a short term sheet (v3) after you confirm which path you want us to price in detail.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Torres <maya@cloudvest.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>, ProcureOps <procureops@cloudvest.com>
Date: 2026-10-23T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — pricing flexibility and credits

Maya / ProcureOps — thanks for the quick turn. Based on procurement feedback and Monica’s operational notes, here’s the agreed commercial pathway and next steps we’ll put into the term sheet for signature: 

Agreed commercial summary (to be captured in the final term sheet):
- Term: 24 months (preferred by CloudVest)
- Discount: 16% off list for the committed baseline
- Credits: $150,000 credit bucket; 50% ($75k) available at signature, 50% ($75k) vested at month 12
- Price-hold: 12-month firm price-hold on committed unit price; years 13+ subject to CPI cap 3%
- Invoicing: Net-45, single quarterly invoice (committed + overage lines) per ProcureOps request
- Ops: Dedicated burst pool provisioned in phase 1 with 95th pct latency SLO; details in the SLA addendum
- Security: we’ll attach Redwood’s standard data residency addendum and accept CloudVest’s vendor addendum as a schedule (legal to exchange redlines)

Action items / timeline:
- Rishi: circulate redwood_term_sheet_v3.pdf with the above changes and a DocuSign envelope by tomorrow EOD (10/24).
- Procurement (CloudVest): confirm any redlines to the vendor addendum within 5 business days of receipt.
- Monica: share capacity forecast mapping the credit bucket to the Q3 spikes (deliverable: 10/27).
- Laura: internal approval for the $150k concession is in place; I’ll attach the internal approval memo to the term sheet.

If that reads correctly, I’ll update the term sheet and send over the DocuSign link so legal/procurement can start routing.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this one.
— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: redwood_term_sheet_v3.pdf (updated stub)
